clue.text: Letting it off may put a joker in bad odour

definitions.text: Letting it off may put a joker in bad odour

blocks.clueFragment: Letting it off may put a joker in bad odour
blocks.note: surface reading: some prankster loses favour after a misdeed
setter's reading: a prank device that, once set off, literally makes its user smell bad

explanation.surface: A practical joker has fallen out of favour after letting something off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In bad odour' is an idiom for being disliked, but here the bad odour is real.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a novelty prank capsule that releases a foul smell when broken, the classic schoolboy trick.

clue.text: Corpse moved with difficulty

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a dead body
second meaning: rigid, not moving freely

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a body being shifted; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a dead body and also an adjective for joints that are rigid and awkward to move.

clue.text: Oddly they're in charge, producing prohibitory decree

indicators.note: taking a word oddly means keeping its first, third, fifth letters and so on
one thing set in another sits inside it, surrounded on both sides

blocks.note: to indict is to charge formally with a crime
its odd-numbered letters, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Strangely, those in charge issue a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' reads as one phrase about authority, but 'in' is the container signal and 'charge' alone is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: An interdict is a formal prohibition, especially a court order or church sanction forbidding an action.

clue.text: County side taken apart by Lancs opener - this'll steady the ship

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the first letter is used
a pair taken apart by something has that thing driven between them

blocks.note: Kent is an English county
the edge is the side of something
Lancs is short for Lancashire

explanation.surface: A county cricket side is beaten by a Lancashire opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: L separates KENT and EDGE: KENT + L + EDGE. Lancashire and Kent are both English counties with cricket teams.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentledge is pig iron used as permanent ballast in a ship's hold, keeping the vessel stable.

clue.text: Novel character both of us like

blocks.note: first meaning: the title of Dickens's last completed novel
second meaning: a person whom you and I are both fond of

explanation.surface: An unusual person whom two of us happen to like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it names a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens published this book in 1865; literally the phrase means someone who is a friend to each of us.

clue.text: Given place in regular army and made to conform

blocks.note: first meaning: put into the line, the regular infantry regiments
second meaning: forced into agreement or obedience

explanation.walkthrough: The regiments of the line were the regular army's infantry, as opposed to guards or militia.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means persuaded or compelled to follow the rules, like soldiers dressed in a straight rank.

clue.text: Seed with appeal for this bird

blocks.note: a pip is a fruit seed
'it' is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone offers a seed to tempt a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small brown songbird of open country, related to wagtails.

clue.text: Parking behind elevated part of plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, something elevated is raised, so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: P is the sign for parking
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: A car is parked at the back of a raised section of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word putting P last, but it is the synonym. 'Plant' suggests a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Each coloured segment of a flower's corolla is one of these, a part of a plant.

clue.text: Idle endlessly in Pennsylvania square

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
one thing set in another sits inside it, surrounded on both sides

blocks.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
lazy means idle

explanation.surface: Loafing around forever in a town square in Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town, especially in Spanish-speaking places.

clue.text: Surprise diversion intended, say, for therapy

indicators.note: what we say is spoken, so the word is judged by its pronunciation

blocks.note: a treat is an unexpected pleasure or outing
intended means meant

explanation.surface: A surprise distraction was meant to be therapeutic.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical care given to a patient for an illness or injury is called treatment, much like therapy.

clue.text: Priest, possibly, backed religious work in secret

definitions.note: 'possibly' marks a priest as one example of someone who intones

indicators.note: something backed is moved in the reverse direction, so the letters run right to left
one thing set in another sits inside it, surrounded on both sides

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament
inner thoughts are private or secret

explanation.surface: A clergyman secretly turned out some religious writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest chants or recites prayers in a monotone during services, so he is one kind of person who intones.

clue.text: Gross offence not in fashion

blocks.note: out is the opposite of in
the rage is the current craze or fashion

explanation.surface: Something hideously unfashionable counts as a gross offence.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is a shocking, flagrant wrong or atrocity that causes indignation.

clue.text: Some prefer a lion in the wild state

indicators.note: taking only some of the following words means a run of letters lifted from inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: Some people would rather see a lion out in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Feral describes animals living untamed, especially domestic species that have reverted to wildness.

clue.text: A French worker, nursing bitterness, is churlish

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close within your arms

blocks.note: un is French for a
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker
gall is bile, and so bitterness or rancour

explanation.surface: A French labourer harbouring resentment behaves rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make 'nursing bitterness' look like an aside about the worker; it is the instruction to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungallant means discourteous, especially lacking chivalry towards women, close to rude or boorish.

clue.text: Chord one found in a form of jazz

indicators.note: what is found in something lies inside it, enclosed by it

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
trad is traditional jazz

explanation.surface: A musician spots a particular chord in a jazz style.
explanation.walkthrough: Trad jazz is the revivalist New Orleans style popular in 1950s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In music theory a triad is a three-note chord built from a root, third and fifth.

clue.text: Seductive woman needs to work sometimes on hair

blocks.note: to temp is to work in temporary jobs now and then
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A seductress has to work on her hair now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A temptress is a woman who sets out to seduce or allure others, a femme fatale.

clue.text: Powerless to limit number? It's indefensible

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in by boundaries on each side

blocks.note: unable means lacking the power to do something
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Being unable to cap some figure is a position nobody can defend.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue; the first half is all wordplay and 'indefensible' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An untenable position cannot be held or justified against attack or criticism.

clue.text: Go miles on converted coinage

indicators.note: something converted is changed into a different form, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A car runs many more miles after its engine conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coinage' suggests money, but it means coining a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly invented word or expression, and coining words produces a coinage.

clue.text: A short dance initially – what we hear is like a stringed instrument

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the word loses its last letter
what we hear is a sound, so the words are judged by pronunciation

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance
taken as written
these two words spoken run together

explanation.surface: A brief dance tune at the start sounds like a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: BAL(L) + A come first ('initially'), then 'like a' said aloud as LAIKA.
explanation.definitionFit: The balalaika is a Russian folk instrument with a triangular body and usually three strings.

clue.text: Spiced liquor left eight men drunk

indicators.note: drunk people stagger about in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spiced drink left eight men intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Metheglin is a spiced or medicated mead, a traditional Welsh alcoholic drink made with honey.

clue.text: Duck, wife allowed, is a small bird

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O
W is the abbreviation for wife
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A husband permits a duck, which turns out to be a little bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young or small owl, so it can be described as a little bird.

clue.text: Popular success in hotter parts up to that time

indicators.note: something split into parts is broken up and can be reassembled differently
one thing set in another sits inside it, surrounded on both sides

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged
a hit is a popular success

explanation.surface: A popular success arrives in the warmer regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up to that time' sits at the end as the definition; 'parts' looks like a noun for regions but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Thitherto is an archaic adverb meaning until then, the past counterpart of hitherto.

clue.text: Hint given clearly, though not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: simply means plainly or clearly

explanation.surface: A hint was given plainly, though not right away.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to suggest something indirectly rather than stating it outright.

clue.text: Alluring woman appearing in the first sixty minutes?

blocks.note: an hour has sixty minutes
Roman numeral one, for first

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman turns up within the first hour.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sixty minutes is hour one: HOUR + I.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is a beautiful maiden of the Muslim paradise, hence any voluptuous, alluring woman.

clue.text: Fuel transporter loses possible user's first letter

indicators.note: what loses something gives it up, so a letter is dropped from the word
names which letter goes: the one at the very front

blocks.note: a boiler is a likely consumer of fuel, hence 'possible user'

explanation.surface: A fuel tanker loses the opening letter of some customer.
explanation.walkthrough: BOILER drops its first letter B. 'Possible user' links back to the fuel: a boiler burns it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a tanker ship that carries oil, so it transports fuel.

clue.text: Laid down, as lines may be

blocks.note: first meaning: decreed, as by an authority
second meaning: drawn straight with a ruler, as on paper

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is descriptive: lines on writing paper are this.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means decided by authority, and it also describes paper marked with straight parallel guide lines.

clue.text: Take up art in Paris, beginning to paint river

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: French es means (thou) art
the opening letter of paint
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Someone takes up painting in Paris, starting with a riverside scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the old verb form (thou art), and in French 'tu es', so ES; it is not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt or champion it, which is to take it up.

clue.text: Character the others follow

blocks.note: surface reading: a leader whom everyone else trails after
setter's reading: a letter of a word, the one that all the other letters come after

explanation.surface: A natural leader is the person everyone else follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but it means a written letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of a word or name is the one standing at the front, with every other letter after it.

clue.text: Old writing instruments, say, rest alongside pen

indicators.note: what we say is spoken, so the words are judged by their pronunciation

blocks.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: Antique pens are described as resting beside a modern pen.
explanation.walkthrough: STY + LIE pronounced together gives the plural of stylus, pronounced 'sty-lie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Styli, plural of stylus, were pointed tools used to write on wax tablets in ancient times.

clue.text: Utopian place for the retired?

blocks.note: surface reading: an ideal haven for pensioners
setter's reading: people who have retired to bed and fallen asleep

explanation.surface: An ideal community for people who have stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' means gone to bed, not stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the imaginary world of sleep and dreams, also an unreal idyllic place.
